fields.Front: What gap does use case modelling bridge?
fields.Back: Between what the system needs to do (requirements) and how the system will achieve it (design).

fields.Text: The four elements of a use case model: {{c1::System}}, {{c2::Actors}}, {{c3::Use Cases}}, {{c4::Relationships}}.

fields.Front: In use case modelling, what is the 'system'?
fields.Back: What you are developing (game, app, website, software); every system has a goal.
Something that uses the system to achieve a goal: usually a person, but also an organization or external device.

fields.Front: What does it mean that actors are 'categorical' and 'external'?
fields.Back: Categorical: they are roles, not individuals (Person, not Michael; Bank, not RBC). External: they sit outside the system boundary.
Primary actor initiates system use; secondary actor is reactionary (responds to the system).
An action to accomplish a certain task within a system, drawn as an oval with a verb phrase.
A connection between an actor and a use case (solid line).
A use case always includes another; dashed arrow labelled <<include>> from the base use case to the included one.
A use case optionally adds behavior to another; dashed arrow labelled <<extend>> from the extending use case to the base.
A specialized use case inherits from another; hollow-headed arrow from the specialized use case to the general one.

fields.Front: In the Banking App diagram, who are the actors?
In the Banking App diagram, what does 'Log in' include and what extends it?
fields.Back: Includes 'Verify password'; extended by 'Display login error'.

fields.Front: In the Banking App diagram, which use cases include 'Verify sufficient funds'?
In the Banking App diagram, which use cases specialize 'Make payment'?

fields.Back: Analyze user interactions from gathered requirements; focus on user goals (e.g., 'Borrow Book', 'Return Book'); look for recurring activities involving the system.

fields.Front: How should use cases be prioritized?
fields.Back: Most important/high-impact first ('Borrow Book' over 'Renew Book'); consider risk—high-risk or complex use cases may need to be addressed earlier.

fields.Text: Use case relationships: {{c1::Include}} = always includes another; {{c2::Extend}} = optionally adds behavior; {{c3::Generalization}} = specialized use case inherits from another.
A {{c1::primary}} actor initiates system use; a {{c2::secondary}} actor is reactionary.
